reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement - arginine levels were depleted from baseline 49-62 μM to 2-9 μM by day 4, confirming ADI-PEG 20 successfully depleted its target substrate arginine. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Clear evidence of downstream pathway modulation - plasma citrulline increased from 23-38 μM to 158-280 μM by day 4-15, confirming the arginine deiminase mechanism was active and converting arginine to citrulline as expected. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Complete failure at clinical translation - 0/31 patients achieved complete or partial response across all three dose cohorts. Primary endpoint of clinical tumor response was not met. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: ASS-negative tumors (the theoretically sensitive population) showed no improved response versus ASS ≤5% positive tumors, indicating the biomarker-defined population strategy failed. Some patients achieved stable disease (9/31, 29%) but no objective responses. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This was a dose-escalation Phase I study with adequate sample size (n=31) and appropriate duration (52 weeks). Safety was manageable with 3.2% grade 5 events. The failure appears mechanistic rather than due to trial design issues.

failure_modes.evidence: Clear target engagement (arginine depletion) and pathway modulation (citrulline increase) confirmed, but 0/31 patients achieved objective response. The mechanism worked biochemically but failed to translate to clinical benefit.
